title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Last $6.56 week (2026-09-28) sold at 54% of baseline. No promotion. Past promotions at lower price lifted sales x1.25 avg. Price hike likely reduces demand; effect shrunk to -20% due to limited evidence.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 44.9. Price increased 2.3% to $6.56 (from $6.41). No events or promotions planned. Recent weeks at $6.56 show mixed results: 24 units (2026-09-28) and 53 (2026-10-05), both vs baseline. The $6.56 price was last seen in 2026-09-28, which sold at 54% of baseline (x0.54). That was an outlier week with no driver. Past promotions at $6.41 averaged x1.57 lift, but noise-adjusted x1.25. No past promotion at $6.56. Price increase likely suppresses demand. Classical model suggests no uplift, but judgment overrides that. Use noise-adjusted price sensitivity: prior $6.56 week was weak, and no promotion to offset. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence. Downside spread widens due to uncertainty in price effect.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.9 | 5%-95%: 20.2 - 68.2 | 10%-90%: 26.8 - 64.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
